lc_person: Balázs Majtényi, ELTE professor working on law, human rights and social history; coauthor of A Contemporary History of Exclusion.
item_person: Balázs Majtényi, jurist and ELTE academic, identified by the same LC, VIAF, GND, ISNI and institutional ORCID identifiers.

evidence.says: Names Majtényi, Balázs; cites Merre visz az út? (2003) and an ELTE profile identifying the professor and his law, human-rights and social-history research. Records birth year 1971 from DNB in VIAF. Links Q112343751, VIAF 28915770, GND 1176538217 and ISNI 0000000037996391.

Labels the item Balázs Majtényi and describes a jurist. Birth statements agree on 1974. Lists LC n2003118394, VIAF 28915770, GND 1176538217, ISNI 0000000037996391 and ORCID 0000-0003-1277-0689; the year-only birth statement cites Czech authority jo20211125802.

Czech National Library authority jo20211125802 has heading Majtényi, Balázs, 1974-, identifies a jurist and historian working on human rights and social history, and gives the matching ORCID and ISNI. Its sources explicitly attribute the authorized name and birth year to OSZK, consulted 13 September 2021.

ELTE identifies Majtényi Balázs as a professor in its Institute of Political and International Studies and Department of Human Rights and Politics. Lists ORCID 0000-0003-1277-0689 and research in constitutional law, human rights, minority rights and social history.
The graph’s Open Library author OL8255635A is credited with Contemporary History of Exclusion, work OL21585734W, alongside a second author.

The publisher lists Balázs Majtényi and György Majtényi as authors of A Contemporary History of Exclusion (2016). Its author biography places Balázs Majtényi at the Institute for Legal Studies and ELTE Faculty of Social Sciences, matching the LC person.

The GND record gives 1971 but identifies the ELTE academic and legal researcher, links the same LC, VIAF, Wikidata, ISNI and ORCID identifiers, and thus concerns the same person despite the conflicting year.

notes: The identity match is strong; the discrepancy concerns the birth year. Prefer 1974, supported by the Czech national authority citing OSZK and consistent with ELTE catalogue headings. LC and GND retain conflicting 1971 dates. No replacement QID is needed.
